body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We tested clean and conflicting saved quality records. Freshly imported works had zero working steps. FORMALCHECK blocked them until the operator checked the effective settings and assigned the matching TECCUT row. GRAFICHECK then confirmed the cut paths and offsets. Reimporting the same job created a separate work with zero steps and preserved the earlier released work.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ba5ff0ae123a87310a475692447f93a841d581a5 -->
Safety-tier review (read-only, not built). Scope: the #2984 delta `feb802a77..ba5ff0ae1` (commits 9b7c4e118, e33017b42, ba5ff0ae1). The parent stack (#2993 and earlier) is part of this diff against `main`, but this review does not cover it.

**Verdict for the #2984 delta: no blockers. Two items are owed (below).**

**Trial merge:** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main ba5ff0ae1` is clean.

**Is the fix correct and complete for #2984?**
- The work-index names `QN2`..`QN10` are gone. One piece quality is registered (`CCB030` or `CCB035`), and its handle is assigned to each work (`crates/post/src/agie/jescript.rs:59`, `:129`).
- The post cannot prove that the control binds the requested tuple, because a resident record with the same name can still win. The PR does not claim that it can. It removes `ASAGIE` and writes `ASDELETE` for each work (`jescript.rs:74-81`). Thus no work has erosion steps on import, and FORMALCHECK blocks the job until the operator assigns TECCUT.
- A stale binding can therefore not cut silently. The output is not silent: the receipt has `working_steps_generated: false` and `controller_review` (`crates/app/src/script/report.rs:83-84`). The GUI status shows the review text (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4681-4684`). The text names the quality, the tuple, the height and the required offsets for each step.
- `stop_on_error` stops the JEScript after `JE_CreateQuality`, `JE_Create`, the `ID_QUALITY` assignment and each `ASDELETE`.
- The mixed-quality group refusal is new (`crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs:162-164`). Mixed stock is already refused at `mod.rs:173-174`, so one height for the review text is correct.
- The remaining risk is the operator step. The decision file and the user guide say this honestly. Only a test on a real control can close it, and the PR says that no physical cut was made.

**Goldens:** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/CCSEP20.SBL` changed. Each change is intended and explained: one `JE_CreateQuality` before the group, the error checks, and no `ASAGIE`. The ISO geometry files did not change.

**Tests that pin the delta:**
- `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs`: `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour` asserts that there is no `ASAGIE`.
- `crates/post/src/agie/tests/group.rs`: `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality` asserts one quality, the handle on each work before the reset, and one `ASDELETE` for each work.
- `crates/app/tests/agie_group.rs`: `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`.
- `crates/app/tests/agie_native.rs`: `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero` asserts the review offsets at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm.
- `crates/app/tests/agie_quality.rs`: `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality` asserts `CCB035`, the offsets and `working_steps_generated === false` through the CLI.

**Owed items:**
1. Add a pin for the new refusal `All works in an Agie group must use the same qualified wire condition` (`mod.rs:163`). The test must assert the message and that no file is written in the destination. Today the `FinePlusRa035` check at `mod.rs:153-158` catches each mixed group first, so this arm cannot be reached. If you keep it as a guard for future qualities, say so in a comment, or let a test call it directly.
2. The PR body gives test counts but no commands or test names for the gate. Add the gate command (for example `cargo xtask gate quick`) and the names of the pinning tests above.

**Rules:**
- Clean-room: no vendor text was found in the delta. The provenance lines are present (`quality.rs`, `jescript.rs:1`, `mod.rs:1`). The MIT notice for Agie Processor is in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.
- The delta adds no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. `unreachable!()` is only in a test match (`agie_native.rs`).
- File sizes in the delta are 400 lines or fewer. `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (1655) and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` were already too large on `main`, and this PR adds only a few lines to them.

**For the maintainer (outside the delta, from the stack):** this PR goes to `main` with the full parent stack. That is about 100 files: a new machine, a new post crate module, geometry modules, and new dependencies in `crates/post/Cargo.toml` (`tempfile`, `rustix`, `windows-sys` as normal dependencies). New dependencies need the owner's decision. Each parent PR needs its own safety-tier review before this head can merge.

Thank you for this fix. The safety-tier review (comment 7052658726) finds the #2984 change itself sound.

The maintainer asks for one change in the shape of the PR:

- This head contains the full unmerged Agie stack (#2948, #2951, #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969, #2972, #2974, #2979, #2981, #2992, #2993). That is about 100 files. Each of those PRs needs its own safety-tier review first.
- Please put the #2984 fix on a branch from `main` alone, without the 12 Agie feature PRs. Then this P1 fix can merge first.

Two small items are owed on the fix:

1. A pinning test for the refusal "All works in an Agie group must use the same qualified wire condition" (`crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs:163`). The test must assert the message and that no file is written. Today an earlier check refuses a mixed group first. Show the case where this refusal is the one that fires, or remove the check.
2. The PR body must give the gate command and the names of the tests that ran.

The new dependencies in `crates/post/Cargo.toml` (`tempfile`, `rustix`, `windows-sys`) need the maintainer's decision only if they stay in the fix.

The separate contribution from main is #3104. Its only parent branch is main. It adds a usable Rust encoder for a complete zero-step SBL and matching SBR for an existing ISO. It adds no dependencies. Its final head passed all 107 quick steps. The exact encoded files created a new punch with zero erosion steps in a copy of the actual control. FORMALCHECK blocked machining until the operator assigns technology.

Main currently has no native Agie workspace post. The original first writer adds a separate publication path that bypasses the generic post output. A change on main alone cannot remove automatic erosion steps from that future path. For that reason #3104 uses Refs #2984. Keep the issue open until the first writer uses this encoder.

The first writer in #2951 is being tested with the separate encoder as its only native setup writer. It retains its existing rectangular-punch and clearance limits. Each later feature still needs its own safety-tier review.

Commit 1fe8950ae addresses the mixed-condition finding here. The two input orders now reach the same specific refusal. The test checks the exact message and the empty destination. All 19 native writer tests passed. The PR body now lists the commands and pinning tests. This integrated draft remains available for review of its feature deltas.

Both screenshots show the same synthetic cutoff job, DEMO2999, after the desktop Post command. The new receipt lists the control checks and the offsets of 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.

Coordinator decision (recorded, unattended):

- This PR does not build on `main` alone. Its head `814dca499` contains the Agie stack commits up to #2993. `main` has no `crates/post/src/agie/`, so a takeover onto `main` is not possible.
- The defect of #2984 is in Agie code that is not on `main`. No post on `main` can emit the wrong output today.
- Chosen: this PR is stacked on #2993. It merges with the Agie stack, after #2951 and the other stack PRs, and is gated then.
- Dropped: a takeover branch onto `main` (17 modify/delete conflicts), and a merge of this PR before its stack.
- The `P1` label stays. Only the maintainer lowers it.

Priority lowered from P1 to P6, the priority of its stack parent #2993. Main has no Agie post, so main cannot emit the defect of #2984. This PR merges after #2993, as the coordinator's comment says. See the comment on #2984.
